source_documents.title: A Solid-State-Emissive 1,8-Naphthalimide Probe Based on Photoinduced Electron Transfer and Aggregation-Induced Emission

reference_evidence_units.quote: the emission was switched “on” increasing the quantum yield of 1 at pH 6.8 to Φ=0.528.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 aqueous pH response
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Water 1e-5 M, excitation 360 nm, Fig. 1; pH 10 to 6.8.
reference_evidence_units.statement: QY rises from 0.024 at pH 10 to 0.528 at 6.8; intensity enhancement 22.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state protonation-dependent response, not direct electron-transfer rate or ESIPT.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PET from the free amine electron pair to the core fluorophore was feasible.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Neutral amine at alkaline pH versus protonated receptor.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors propose amine-to-fluorophore PET quenching in base and suppression upon protonation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Source calls protonated species a quaternary ammonium cation; that terminology is not adopted as chemical-graph verification.

reference_evidence_units.quote: PET switching mechanism takes place from pH 10 to pH 7.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 solution titration
reference_evidence_units.statement: Switching occurs over pH 10-7 with fitted pKa reported as 8.50 +/- 0.08.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Not the paper-strip pH window; main text refers to SI selectivity controls that were not inspected.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a well pronounced green AIE fluorescence (Figure S5) centred at 525 nm
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 concentration dependence
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Concentrated solution compared with dilution; main reports SI Figs. S5-S7.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Concentrated samples show 525 nm band that diminishes on dilution toward approximately 400 nm monomer emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Detailed concentrations/spectra in SI not inspected; do not invent aggregation threshold.

reference_evidence_units.quote: according to the Kasha’s exciton theory with formation of J-aggregates.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 aggregate interpretation
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Discussion of target red-shifted aggregate band by analogy with previously reported 4-chloro naphthalimides.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors invoke prior J-aggregate/exciton explanation for the red-shifted target aggregate emission.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Analogy-based interpretation, not target diffraction or direct excitonic splitting measurement; Kasha exciton theory is not anti-Kasha emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The obtained film was exposed successively for 2 seconds to HCl and NH3 vapours.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 glass film
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Acetonitrile sprayed on glass, evaporated in air; Figs. 2-3 visually inspected.
reference_evidence_units.statement: HCl produces bright emission and subsequent NH3 returns it to low emission within the reported 2 s exposure protocol.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Vapor dose is not quantified; this does not establish cycling durability or aqueous pKa of the film.

reference_evidence_units.quote: with maxima at 472 nm for 1 and 480 nm for 2
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 with comparator 2
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Solid films after HCl exposure; 360 nm excitation.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Target broad film emission peaks at 472 nm with enhancement 44; comparator 2 peaks at 480 nm with enhancement 48.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Authors describe combined monomer and aggregate emission; comparator values must not replace target values.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The better expressed AIE emission in 1 and 2 could be attributed to the hydrogen bonding ability
reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 and comparator 2 versus 3
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Ethanolamine-bearing 1/2 compared with dimethylamine 3 in solids.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Authors tentatively attribute stronger aggregate emission to OH/NH hydrogen-bonding ability.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No target packing structure or motion measurement; retained as bounded packing-interaction interpretation, not automatic RIM.

reference_evidence_units.subject: compound 1 on paper
reference_evidence_units.conditions: Acetonitrile-loaded filter paper dried and exposed to aqueous solutions; Fig. 4.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Paper-supported fluorescence switching requires strongly acidic conditions, unlike solution pH 10-7.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Authors leave detailed thermodynamic origin for future work; matrix context is observed but mechanism unresolved.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compound 2 is well soluble in water
reference_evidence_units.subject: nonchlorinated compound 2 control
reference_evidence_units.statement: Comparator 2 migrates rapidly into water; chlorinated target 1 paper is more stable, which source attributes to increased hydrophobicity.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Comparator solubility is not target aggregation or direct binding evidence.

reference_mechanisms.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Tentative hydrogen-bond-mediated aggregate emission and support-dependent response; exact heterogeneous equilibrium remains unresolved.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Source explicitly proposes protonation-controlled PET in solution and solid film; no claim of direct transient proof.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Preserve authors analogy-based J-aggregate explanation and mixed monomer/aggregate film emission, with limited target-specific structural evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific restriction of intramolecular motion is established in the selected evidence; aggregation alone is insufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: PACKING_HOST_MATRIX_CONFINEMENT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Tentative hydrogen-bond-mediated aggregate emission and support-dependent response; exact heterogeneous equilibrium remains unresolved.

mechanism_decisions.label: HOST_GUEST_INTERACTION
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target host-guest binding mechanism is established; ordinary solvent polarity is not host inclusion.

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific charge-transfer excited-state assignment is established in the selected evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: ESIPT_PT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No excited-state proton-transfer photophysics is established. Ground-state protonation or hydrogen bonding alone is insufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Source explicitly proposes protonation-controlled PET in solution and solid film; no claim of direct transient proof.

mechanism_decisions.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Preserve authors analogy-based J-aggregate explanation and mixed monomer/aggregate film emission, with limited target-specific structural evidence.

mechanism_decisions.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No distinct radiative-rate or bright/dark-state balance mechanism is established beyond the other pathways; intensity and lifetime alone are insufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: TRIPLET_METAL_ENERGY_TRANSFER
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific triplet, metal-centered or energy-transfer pathway is established; metal binding alone is insufficient.

mechanism_decisions.label: RACI_CI_ACCESS
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No target-specific conical-intersection access mechanism is established.

mechanism_decisions.label: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA
mechanism_decisions.rationale: No higher-state emission or suppression of Kasha's rule is established.
